questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix and $p=\min(m,n)$. How are the singular values $\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_p\ge0$ of $A$ defined?
options: As the square roots of the largest $p$ eigenvalues of $A^{\top}A$
As the absolute values of the eigenvalues of $A$
As the largest $p$ eigenvalues of $A^{\top}A$ themselves
As the square roots of the eigenvalues of $A$

questions.question: For a real $m\times n$ matrix $A$, why are all eigenvalues of $A^{\top}A$ nonnegative, so that their square roots, the singular values, are real?
options: Because $A^{\top}A$ is symmetric, and symmetric matrices have nonnegative eigenvalues
Because the entries of $A^{\top}A$ are sums of squares, hence all nonnegative

questions.question: Which statement correctly contrasts the singular values of a real matrix $A$ with its eigenvalues?
options: Singular values, like eigenvalues, need $A$ to be square
Singular values, like eigenvalues, may be complex numbers
Singular values exist for any $m\times n$ $A$ and are real and nonnegative
Singular values and eigenvalues agree up to sign for square $A$

questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix. Which quantity equals the number of positive singular values of $A$?
options: The number of nonzero eigenvalues of $A$ (for square $A$)

questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix with largest singular value $\sigma_1$. What does $\sigma_1$ measure?
options: The largest absolute value of an eigenvalue of $A$
The largest length $\|A\boldsymbol{x}\|$ over unit vectors $\boldsymbol{x}$
The largest absolute value of an entry of $A$
The factor $|\det A|$ by which $A$ scales volume

questions.question: What are the singular values $\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2$ of $A=\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&-4\end{pmatrix}$?
What are the singular values $\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2$ of $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&2\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, whose eigenvalues are both $0$?
Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$, so $A^{\top}A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&8\end{pmatrix}$; the eigenvalues of $A$ are not real. What are the singular values of $A$?
options: None real, as $A$ has complex eigenvalues

questions.question: Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&0&2\end{pmatrix}$, a $2\times3$ matrix. Using the smaller product $AA^{\top}$, what are its singular values $\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2$?
Let $Q$ be a $2\times2$ orthogonal matrix. What are the singular values of $-3Q$?
A real $2\times5$ matrix $A$ has singular values $\sigma_1=4$, $\sigma_2=1$. What are the positive singular values of the $5\times2$ matrix $A^{\top}$?
options: Unknown, as $AA^{\top}$ and $A^{\top}A$ differ in size

questions.question: For which matrix are the singular values exactly the absolute values of its eigenvalues?
Let $A$ be a real $n\times n$ matrix. Which transformation of $A$ always leaves all singular values unchanged?
A real $3\times3$ matrix $A$ has singular values $5$, $2$ and $\tfrac{1}{2}$. What are $|\det A|$ and the sum of the squares of all entries, $\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}^2$?
What are the singular values $\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2$ of the rank-one matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\4&0\end{pmatrix}$?
A real $3\times2$ matrix $A$ has singular values $\sigma_1=4$ and $\sigma_2=1$. Which value cannot occur as $\|A\boldsymbol{x}\|$ for a unit vector $\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2$?
A real $m\times n$ matrix $A$ with $m\ge n$ has singular values $\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_n\ge0$. What are the singular values of the symmetric $n\times n$ matrix $A^{\top}A$?
options: $\sqrt{\sigma_1},\ldots,\sqrt{\sigma_n}$: one more square root of each value

questions.question: $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&1\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}$ ($2\times3$) has singular values $\sigma_1=\sqrt{2}$, $\sigma_2=1$. What is $\min\|A\boldsymbol{x}\|$ over unit vectors $\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^3$?
Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&0\\2&1\end{pmatrix}$, a $3\times2$ matrix with no eigenvalues. What are its singular values $\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2$?
For which real $a$ does $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&a\end{pmatrix}$ have a zero singular value?
options: No $a$, since singular values are positive
